cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Everything Is a Contest
cards.instruction: Turn every difference or disagreement into a competition you intend to win.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. My tea's stronger than yours. I can handle it without milk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Same teapot. I added milk so I could drink mine sooner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. First to finish, then. I've only got two mouthfuls left.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fewest refills wins, then. I can make these two mouthfuls last all breakfast.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 and A3 authority claims are detachable from A5 ordinary metric switching, which does not treat B contribution as permission.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 same-teapot correction causes A3 speed contest; B4 finished cup causes A5 refill contest, but A3 delays a question never asked.

relationship.evidence: B2 explains a practical milk choice and B4 simply makes more tea, giving A everyday differences to turn competitive.

heightening.evidence: B4 has already won speed, so A5 makes remaining tea an endurance advantage.

specificity.evidence: A1 tea difference, B2 shared pot and A3 two mouthfuls establish consistent quantities and activity.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 breakfast-long endurance is earned by B4 refill; A3 stock command disrupts otherwise compact speech.
